title.narrative: Strengthening Fiscal, Financial, and Economic Resilience Subprogram 1

description.narrative:
Mongolia's current growth trajectory is a critical period to implement and accelerate structural reforms. More specifically, these reforms should address challenges related to strengthening public financial management, the finance sector, and the role of the private sector in the quest for economic diversification.
The proposed program comprises a set of complementary medium-term structural reforms, focused on strengthening the country's fiscal, finance sector, and economic resilience against the impact of exogenous shocks. More specifically, the program supports medium-term reforms focused on (i) improving domestic resource mobilization, by leveraging a critical set of tax administration and tax policy reforms; (ii) boosting debt sustainability through improving debt management and the management of sovereign liability risks; (iii) improving finance sector stability and resilience through strengthened banking sector supervision and regulation, enhancing NPL resolution, and promoting financial consumer protection; and (iv) strengthening the upstream environment for private sector development through relevant legal reforms, support for public private partnerships; and reforms focused on turning the Development Bank of Mongolia into an institution with a viable value proposition and operating model.

Reports and Recommendations of the President

1. In line with the MTA’s Mid-Term Strategy 2021–2024, approved by MOF to align Mongolia’s tax administration with internationally established good practices: • MTA’s 2022 Tax Compliance Program implemented, resulting in a reduced compliance risk across the spectrum of taxpayers (micro, small, medium, and large). By July 2023, MTA initiated the collection of sex-disaggregated data across all taxpayer categories (micro, small, medium, and large), ensuring gender-inclusive Tax Compliance Program. • MTA’s 2022 Tax Literacy Program implemented, resulting in full readiness for the nationwide roll-out of a Tax Literacy Program, focused on improved submission of voluntary tax obligations. • MTA’s 2022 Tax Digitization Program implemented, resulting in increased use of ICT solutions in the tax administration (addressing strengthened risk management, improved tax compliance and improved data analytics skills in MTA).

2. MTA enhanced TAIS to enable the generation of sex-disaggregated tax data to promote gender-inclusion in tax administration operations. (i) By July 2023, a technical assessment on TAIS’s sex-disaggregated data collection and generation completed. (ii) By July 2023, completion of sex-disaggregated data collection and analytics capacity building training for MTA ITC staff achieved, with a minimum of 45% women participation. (iii) By July 2023, a sample sex-disaggregated data report (including women-owned MSMEs) generated by TAIS.

3. Mongolia aligned its tax policy and administration with two key international taxation treaties: • it signed the Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (the BEPS Convention) • it formally committed to implementing the International Standard for the Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information in Tax Matters by 2026. (Status of Commitments)
4. MTA’s 2024 Tax Compliance Program shall have been implemented, resulting in early detection of tax avoidance across specified categories of taxpayers, contributing to improved compliance.

5. MTA’s 2024 nation-wide roll-out of Tax Literacy Program shall have been implemented. (i) By July 2025, tax literacy training for at least 1,100 high school students (with participation of at least 50% girls) in nine districts of Ulaanbaatar shall have been organized (collect and report sex-disaggregated data). (ii) By July 2025, tax literacy and compliance training specifically for MSMEs, with a minimum of 45% women participation and the participation of 30% women owned MSMEs shall have been organized. (iii) By July 2025, an impact assessment of MTA’s Tax Literacy Program shall have been completed, ensuring a minimum of 50% women respondents and 30% women-owned MSME respondents in the assessment.
6. MTA’s 2024 Tax Digitization Program shall have been implemented.

7. Sex-disaggregated tax data reporting shall have been integrated to TAIS, and tax-related gender statistics shall have been made available to public. (i) By July 2025, a capacity building training program on data analytics, data cleaning, data mart and data administration for MTA ICT staff shall have been implemented (with participation of at least 45% women). (ii) By July 2025, “Gender and tax” data section shall have been integrated into the TAIS as a submenu (MTA internal use). (iii) By July 2025, tax-related gender statistics and infographics including women-owned MSMEs, shall have been made publicly available on the official website www.mta.gov.mn.

8. Gender responsive tax policy design and tax administration services for women-owned MSMEs shall have been completed. (i) By July 2025, a gender analysis to identify tax issues/barriers and evaluate impact of tax policies and regulations to women-owned MSMEs shall have been completed. (ii) By July 2025, a proposal to improve tax services for women-owned MSMEs shall have been submitted to Ministry of Finance.

9. MOF shall have implemented the BEPS Convention and shall have all necessary preparations in place for the implementation of the International Standard for the Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information in Tax Matters by 2026. (Status of Commitments)
